obligation: Bank recall request for a diverted payment
trigger: A payment (ACH or wire) is suspected to have gone to an account controlled by an attacker
deadline: Immediately on suspicion. IC3: 'time is of the essence'; request a recall and any indemnification documents
notify: The company's bank (outbound payments); ask the owner to call its own bank (inbound payments)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - practical step, not a legal duty. Highest priority action in this runbook

obligation: Complaint to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
trigger: Any business email compromise with a fraudulent transfer or attempt
deadline: As soon as possible, regardless of the amount; IC3 may help freeze funds
notify: IC3 (www.ic3.gov); local FBI field office if the loss is large

trigger: Unauthorized access to personal information of Florida residents. This includes name plus Social Security number, or an email address plus the password that opens the account (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay allowed on written request)
notify: Each affected Florida resident (mail or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the compromised mailbox held personal information, such as certified payrolls with full Social Security numbers. The account holder's own credentials also count

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (15 more days for individual notice if good cause is given in writing within 30 days)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (instead of individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or financial harm
deadline: Document in writing; keep 5 years; give to the Department within 30 days after the determination

obligation: Vendor (third-party agent) breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (for example the payroll provider) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after its determination

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected residents live (some craft workers and subcontractor employees live outside Florida)

obligation: Correct SAM EFT information and alert the federal payment office
trigger: The company's EFT (bank) information in SAM was changed without authorization, or a federal payment is missing
deadline: Immediately. If EFT information was incorrect or revised within 30 days of the Government's release of payment and the funds have left the payment office, the Government is deemed to have paid and the company must recover the funds
notify: SAM (correct the record); Contracting Officer and paying office for each affected contract
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the federal variant of this runbook

obligation: Pay subcontractors on federal contracts despite a diverted payment
trigger: A payment meant for a subcontractor on a federal job went to an attacker
deadline: Subcontractor must still be paid within 7 days of the company's receipt of the Government's payment; interest penalty for late payment
notify: The subcontractor (after call-back verification of its real bank details)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for federal jobs (FC-1 to FC-3)

obligation: DoD cyber incident reporting for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery ('rapidly report'); preserve images 90 days; subcontractors report to DoD and give incident number to prime
notify: DoD via https://dibnet.dod.mil (DoD-approved medium assurance certificate required); malware to DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3)
applies_at_this_tier: Not today: the company holds no covered defense information (P03 G-033). The analysis step confirms no CDI was in the compromised mailbox

obligation: CMMC status currency after an incident
trigger: An incident shows that a CMMC Level 1 requirement is no longer met
deadline: Before relying on the status for any award or making the next annual affirmation; restore compliance and re-assess
applies_at_this_tier: After the company holds Final Level 1 (Self), expected 2026-12-15. The final clause has no separate incident notice duty

obligation: Report discovery of covered telecommunications equipment/services during contract performance
trigger: Covered equipment identified in a system during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered by business email compromise. Listed because the company holds federal contracts (used in August 2026 for FC-1)

obligation: Owner notice of a compromised payment channel
trigger: Any suspicion that an owner received false remittance instructions from a company mailbox or lookalike domain
deadline: Immediately by phone to the owner's AP contact on file, then in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not a statutory duty

trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
deadline: Per policy; social engineering coverage typically requires prompt notice and proof of verification procedures
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not a legal duty. Use the carrier's panel counsel and forensics

citation: General indemnity agreement with the surety (contract)
trigger: A loss large enough to affect working capital or the ability to pay subcontractors

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Construction is not a CISA critical infrastructure sector; recheck when final

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Not for business email compromise (no ransom). Applies only if an extortion demand follows
